idea: Distance-based heavy-lorry charge (Germany Maut: 0.09-0.14 EUR/km for trucks over 12 t by axles and Euro class; UK LRUC for over 3.5 t, possibly by road type and time of day) and a zonal congestion charge (London weekdays 07:00-18:30; predicted 10-15% traffic cut). In route choice terms a toll is an added generalised cost on links.
does: Adds a per-km or per-entry charge by vehicle type on chosen roads/cordon, converts it to time (charge / value of time) in route assignment and mode choice, runs the experiment and reports traffic diversion and revenue
inputs: roads or cordon, charge by vehicle type and time window, value of time
outputs: diverted vehicles, change in flow and delay, revenue
notes: Book gives rates and the 10-15% traffic cut only as reference points for checking a simulated result, not a model.

idea: In the UK heavy lorries are in 8% of trunk-road collisions but 26% of casualties, mainly because of mass and longer stopping distance; ABS cuts rates.
does: Weights analyse_safety conflicts by vehicle class (mass/braking distance) so a run with more trucks shows a heavier severity share, benchmarked at 8% of conflicts vs 26% of casualties
notes: Only two numbers given; weights would be assumptions.

idea: Legal 44 t gross combination, 16.5 m articulated length with 13.6 m semi-trailer, 4 m height limit, tractor takes at least 20% of laden weight, 3+3 axle, 400-500 hp.
does: Sets realistic length (16.5 m), mass (44 t) and power for a Truck/Trailer vehicle type, so car-following gaps, acceleration and PCU of trucks match real articulated lorries
notes: UK/EU specific limits; check against the SUMO trailer defaults before changing.

idea: Combined road-rail cut CO2 by 20 to over 50% in 17 of 19 routes, but is not automatically better: only when the feeder road legs are short or in the direction of travel, or electricity is low-carbon; energy was 15% higher in 3 cases.
does: Screens a proposed truck-to-rail shift using trunk distance vs road feeder distance and detour
inputs: trunk km, feeder km, detour factor, emission factors
outputs: net CO2 change, flag when feeder share too large
notes: Freight rail is outside ACMS; only the feeder-leg road traffic effect is relevant.
